nodes.label: Emotional Feedback Loops
nodes.rationale: Functional feedback alone (green check, red X) is forgettable; pairing actions with encouragement, personality, and proportional celebration creates emotional reinforcement that drives retention.

nodes.label: Peak-End Rule
nodes.rationale: Nobel Prize-winning research by Daniel Kahneman shows the brain compresses an experience into two remembered moments, the peak and the end, so designing those two moments yields disproportionate perceived quality (Disney parks: 70% of visitors return for remembered moments, not a flawless day).

nodes.label: UI Lens vs UX Lens Separation
nodes.norm_label: ui lens vs ux lens separation
nodes.rationale: Gathering UI and UX inspiration separately prevents visual style from biasing structural decisions; visual direction is finalized before wireframing so stakeholder feedback stays about one dimension at a time.

nodes.label: 60/30/10 Color Rule
nodes.rationale: 60% neutral base, 30% complementary, 10% accent reserves strong color for meaningful moments (CTAs, key indicators); overusing accent color kills hierarchy.

nodes.label: Core Design Philosophy (Intentionality)
nodes.rationale: Great mobile UI is not about flashiness but intentionality: every pixel, spacing value, and color must serve the user and the primary goal, making interfaces feel smooth, personal, and alive rather than merely functional.

nodes.label: 8-Point Grid Spacing System
nodes.rationale: All spacing divisible by 8 or 4 plus relationship-based spacing (2x multiplier between groups) creates rhythm and encodes grouping without borders.

nodes.label: Thumb Zone
nodes.rationale: Primary actions belong in the bottom third of the screen because that is where thumbs comfortably reach, minimizing interaction cost on one-handed mobile use.

nodes.label: Typography Hierarchy Rule
nodes.rationale: Limiting to one font family, four sizes, and two weights (using size, weight, and opacity for hierarchy) prevents visual noise and keeps scanning effortless.

nodes.label: Selection Over Manual Input
nodes.rationale: Tappable options for common choices reduce interaction cost and typing errors; icons/emojis add personality, and an 'Other' manual fallback preserves flexibility.

nodes.label: Order/Status Tracking Pattern
nodes.rationale: Open with a confident status message, humanize with photos, names and quick actions, and use visual timelines instead of text date lists because timelines answer 'where is it now' at a glance.

nodes.label: Quick Reference: Design Laws Summary
nodes.rationale: Condenses the framework into Understand -> Structure -> Visual Design -> Emotion -> Polish plus six named laws, intended as the entry point before drilling into detail.

nodes.label: ASO Shots (Store Screenshot Skill)
nodes.rationale: Recommended downstream skill: designed screens become App Store / Google Play screenshots; it writes headlines, offers 3 style directions and exports required sizes (installed via npx skills add ceorkm/aso-shots).

nodes.label: AI/Tech Design Language
nodes.rationale: Soft gradients, moving elements, glowing dimensionality and smooth animations communicate intelligence; ethereal accents on dark or light themes.

nodes.label: 4-Phase Client/Product Design Process
nodes.rationale: Discovery (mood boards by vibe, 3-5 directions) -> UI direction (visual only, client mixes button/typography/cards from options) -> UX structure (brain dump then MVP 3-5 screens, wireframes) -> combine. Deliberately finalizes the visual direction before wireframing so stakeholders are never surprised late.

nodes.label: The Comfort Trap (Consistency as a Moat)
nodes.norm_label: the comfort trap (consistency as a moat)
nodes.rationale: Spotify principle: every interaction follows the same logic so predictable patterns become second nature, raising switching costs. Consistency is framed as habit formation and defensibility, not aesthetics.

nodes.label: Crypto/Web3 Design Language
nodes.rationale: Neon colors, bold typography, dark backgrounds and geometric shapes. Phantom's lesson: polish builds trust, so visual details, motion and transitions are core product features rather than fluff.

nodes.label: Daniel Kahneman (Nobel Prize Peak-End Research)
nodes.rationale: Cited as the authority behind the Peak-End Rule, which is what licenses the whole emotion step of the skill.

nodes.label: E-commerce/Food Design Language
nodes.rationale: High-quality product photography, prominent CTAs and frictionless checkout, backed by trust signals such as reviews, ratings and delivery estimates.

nodes.label: Education/Learning Design Language
nodes.rationale: Bright playful palettes and character-driven personality. Duolingo's lesson is quantitative: character animations plus emotional feedback loops doubled DAUs from 14.2M to 34M+ in two years.

nodes.label: Finance/Banking Design Language
nodes.rationale: Blue-dominant palettes signal trust, stability and reliability; generous white space and conservative typography make it feel safe. Revolut's lesson: tactile interactions (draggable charts, 3D card flips) convert basic features into premium experiences.

nodes.label: Fitness Design Language
nodes.rationale: Energetic colors, bold typography and progress-focused visual momentum, with UI complexity adapted to user stage (new, returning, power user).

nodes.label: Health/Wellness Design Language
nodes.rationale: Bright approachable colors reduce anxiety, friendly illustrations and warm micro-interactions soften the tone, and non-intimidating onboarding matters most. Ahead (Apple Design Award) lesson: guide users kindly and build the peak as a personalized insight moment.

nodes.label: Productivity Design Language
nodes.rationale: Clean minimal yet information-dense layouts, strong grids and consistent spacing, quick actions and keyboard shortcuts for power users.

nodes.label: Sleep/Meditation Design Language
nodes.rationale: Purple and deep blue tones, minimal UI, soft transitions and ambient low-contrast surfaces support calm rather than stimulation.

nodes.label: The Trojan Horse (Hide Complexity in Familiar Interfaces)
nodes.norm_label: the trojan horse (hide complexity in familiar interfaces)
nodes.rationale: Spotify principle: wrap sophisticated features in UI patterns users already know, because users do not want to interact with algorithms - they want experiences that feel natural.

nodes.label: The Vanity Mirror (Sharing as Identity)
nodes.rationale: Spotify principle: celebrate who users are, not what they did in your app. Personal insights should be meaningful enough that sharing feels like self-expression ('You're a night owl...' beats 'You completed 25 tasks').

nodes.label: Mobile Design Anti-Patterns
nodes.rationale: Captured as a checklist so violations are recognizable: flashy gradients, >4 font sizes or >3 weights, off-grid spacing, key content hidden behind banners/taps, CTAs outside the thumb zone, guidance-free empty states, sliders for precise entry, flat visual weight, labels emphasized over values, and gray shadows on colored backgrounds.

nodes.label: Step 4: Design for Emotion (Peak and End)
nodes.norm_label: step 4: design for emotion (peak and end)
nodes.rationale: Only two moments are remembered: the peak and the end. Design the peak with micro-animations, celebratory feedback, sparkles and encouraging copy; design the ending with a summary card, progress affirmation and a gentle nudge to return. Motion doubles as a trust signal in high-stakes domains such as finance, crypto and health.

nodes.label: 5-Step Mobile Design Process
nodes.rationale: Sequenced deliberately: context precedes structure, structure precedes visuals, and emotion/polish come last, so visual decisions are constrained by UX intent instead of decorating an unvalidated layout.

nodes.label: F-Pattern Reading Order
nodes.rationale: Content is laid out along the natural F-shaped scan path so eyes hit the highest-value information without hunting.

nodes.label: Implementation Stack (React, Tailwind, Lucide, Recharts)
nodes.rationale: Chosen so the skill's static rules map onto utility classes and tokens: Tailwind for spacing/color/typography, CSS variables for the color system, Lucide for consistent iconography, Recharts for data viz, CSS transitions for micro-interactions, and a 375px (iPhone SE) mobile-first baseline with rounded-2xl/3xl and backdrop-blur.

nodes.label: Personalization by User Stage
nodes.rationale: New users get a simple welcome and guided setup, returning users get personalized routine-focused content with progress, power users get dense stats and optimization tools; adapting density to stage prevents both overwhelm and boredom.

nodes.label: Step 5: Polish and Details
nodes.rationale: Glow behind key elements (blur + opacity), tiny white inner shadows on primary buttons, 5% primary-color borders, micro-animations, 44x44pt minimum tap targets, contrast checks, and all of error/empty/loading/success states designed. Polish is the difference between functional and alive.

nodes.label: Soft Tinted Shadow Rules
nodes.rationale: Soft shadows only, always tinted to the background hue; subtle white inner shadows on buttons add dimension. Harsh or pure-gray shadows read as cheap and break the color system.

nodes.label: Smarter Search Pattern
nodes.rationale: Never show a blank search screen; always surface recent searches, popular/trending items and personalized recommendations so the empty state still advances the user's goal.

nodes.label: Thumb Zone Placement
nodes.rationale: Primary actions belong in the bottom third of the screen so the core goal is reachable one-handed; placing CTAs outside it is listed as an anti-pattern.

nodes.label: Typography Hierarchy Rules
nodes.rationale: One font family (two max), at most 4 sizes and 2 weights, monospace for metrics, text containers under 600px. Hierarchy is created with size, weight and opacity rather than bolding everything, because uniform weight destroys scannability.

nodes.label: Visual Cues and Imagery Guidance
nodes.rationale: Icons, emojis, illustrations and images make information digestible; for people, avatars/photos beat initials which beat generic icons. Consistent curated or AI-generated visuals with matching palettes, never a random stock-photo mix.

nodes.label: Emotional Feedback Loops
nodes.rationale: Actions should return emotional rather than purely functional feedback: encouragement and character reactions instead of a green check, gentle personality-driven correction instead of a red X, proportional celebration for milestones, and motion-based momentum visualization for progress. The stated reason is that emotional feedback is retained where functional feedback is forgotten.

nodes.label: Peak-End Rule
nodes.rationale: The brain does not store an experience as a whole; it compresses it into the most intense moment (peak) and the final impression (end). Disney parks are cited: 70% of visitors return because of remembered moments, not a flawless day. Applied to apps by mapping the flow, designing ONE 'holy dang' peak after core-task completion or milestone, always giving closure at the end, and reducing negative peaks at wait screens, errors and long forms (using delays as content opportunities).

nodes.label: UI Lens vs UX Lens Separation
nodes.norm_label: ui lens vs ux lens separation
nodes.rationale: UI lens asks how colors work together, what emotions they evoke, spacing, typography and hierarchy; UX lens asks where the search bar is, whether tap targets are big enough, how many steps a core task takes, and what can be eliminated. Mixing the lenses during research corrupts both, so inspiration is gathered separately.

nodes.label: 60/30/10 Color Rule
nodes.rationale: 60% neutral base, 30% complementary, 10% accent. Opacity variations of the neutral (100/80/60-70%) carry text hierarchy, accent at 5% opacity backs secondary buttons, and strong colors such as red are reserved for meaningful moments because overuse kills hierarchy. Shadow colors are tinted to match the background instead of pure gray/black.

nodes.label: Core Design Philosophy (Intentionality Over Flashiness)
nodes.rationale: Great mobile UI is not about flashiness but intentionality: every pixel, spacing value and color must serve the user. Interfaces should feel smooth, personal and alive rather than merely functional. Three pre-design questions: what is the user trying to accomplish, how should this make them feel, and what is the one thing they should notice first.

nodes.label: 8-Point Grid Spacing System
nodes.rationale: All spacing divisible by 8 or 4 (8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96) plus relationship-based spacing: related elements close, unrelated far, and the gap to the next group is 2x the intra-group gap. Larger text needs larger spacing. Section padding 80-96px, card padding 24-32px.
